answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the juniper ordering is published with the voyage batch, the crystal audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 54% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Honest users pay that once, farms 30 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
